literal: In laziness she dwells, the great goddess of misfortune, they say; laziness he who is without, in effort he who is, [his is] she of the lotus.
translation: They say the great goddess of misfortune dwells in laziness. The goddess of the lotus belongs to the man who is free from laziness and steadfast in effort.
modern: சோம்பலில் மூதேவி குடியிருப்பாள் என்று சான்றோர் கூறுவர். ஆனால், சோம்பல் இன்றி முயற்சியில் நிலைத்திருப்பவனிடம் தாமரையில் வீற்றிருக்கும் திருமகள் தங்கியிருப்பாள்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the outcomes of laziness and industriousness using personified imagery. The poet states that the goddess of misfortune ('முகடி') resides in laziness, bringing ruin to the idle. In contrast, the goddess of prosperity, who sits on a lotus ('தாமரையினாள்'), favors the one who is free from laziness and actively engaged in effort. The parallel structure emphasizes that wealth and success are naturally drawn to continuous hard work.
